paper_metadata.title: High-temperature nickel alloys modified with hafnium and zirconium

evidence.quote: In the present work we studied the effect of individual and joint alloying of nickel alloys ZhS6U-VI and ZhS6DK-VI with hafnium and zirconium on the structure and properties of castings.

In the present work we studied the effect of individual and joint alloying of nickel alloys ZhS6U-VI and ZhS6DK-VI with hafnium and zirconium on the structure and properties of castings.

The alloys were fabricated by the method of remelting a measured preform in a UPPF-3M vacuum induction furnace in a 15-kg crucible with a basic lining. 10-30 sec before casting the metal, heated to 1600~ weighed portions of Hf-Ni and Zr-Ni alloying sets were added to it through the charging device of the furnace.
The ultimate rupture strength, the specific elongation, and the impact toughness of the specimens were determined after preliminary air quenching from 1210~ (4hi.

The microstructure of the studied cast alloys consists of dendrites (light zones), interaxial regions (dark zones) (Fig. la ), particles of-},'-phase (intermetallics of the type Ni3(A1, Ti)), carbides, borides, and eutectic (7 + 7')-P base located in interaxial spaces and near grain boundaries.

After vacuum remelting and slow cooling of the castings in the heated ceramic molds, the morphology of the carbides is changed (Fig. 2h ), they are segregated in the fore1 of fihns and "'Chinese hieroglyphs," tbnning a skeleton over grain boundaries, thus diminishing the ductility and long-term strength of the alloys.
